question: Should experimental grouped Claw update planning and its distinct capability-consent model become a maintained OpenClaw core contract once the parent lifecycle stack is ready?
rationale: The patch defines a new core CLI/schema/ownership boundary rather than repairing established behavior; correctness evidence cannot decide whether this permanent product surface belongs in core.

options.title: Sponsor the staged core contract
options.body: Approve the planner direction after parent-stack landing order and current-head secret-safe output proof are reviewed.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Keep only the read-only ownership reconciliation needed by current lifecycle tooling and defer capability-consent presentation to a later approved design.

options.title: Route externally
options.body: Decline the experimental core surface and retain any future grouped-update workflow outside the core product until a narrower seam is approved.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged core contract
recommendation.body: Approve the planner direction after parent-stack landing order and current-head secret-safe output proof are reviewed.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the concrete review requirements for this update-planning boundary and is assigned to the PR.
